title: Problem Set: Real-World Inventory Order Processor
solutionExplanation: Implements full multi-list tail-recursive order fulfillment, total price calculation, and inventory restocking with strict TCO and O(1) stack space.

otpDocCards.complexityNote: Zero-copy garbage collection with bounded O(1) process stack.

mentalModelCheck.question: Why does calculate_order_total/2 return 175 for orders [{order, 1, 2}, {order, 2, 3}, {order, 3, 5}] against products P1($50, stock 10), P2($25, stock 5), and P3($200, stock 2)?

options.label: P1 is fulfilled (2 * 50 = 100), P2 is fulfilled (3 * 25 = 75), but P3 requires 5 when stock is only 2, so P3 is unfulfilled (0), giving 100 + 75 + 0 = 175
options.explanation: Unfulfillable orders contribute 0 to the total order value without halting execution.

options.label: Because the function applies a 10% volume discount across all orders
options.explanation: There are no volume discounts; prices are evaluated directly from inventory.

options.label: P3 raises a badarith exception that is caught by a supervisor
options.explanation: Stock insufficiency is handled purely with pattern matching and guard clauses.
